provenance: Real Kestrix output on a synthetic input generated by scripts/build_landing_samples.py.
score_note: Heuristic score from offline checks of the URL text only; the URL was never visited. It is not a probability of phishing: 0 means none of the checks fired, not that the site is safe.

findings.title: Uses a raw IP address instead of a name
findings.explanation: The link points straight at 203.0.113.9. Genuine organisations almost always use a domain name; phishing pages are often hosted on rented or hacked servers reached by IP address.

findings.title: Text before '@' disguises the real site
findings.explanation: Browsers ignore everything before the '@' ('northbank.example') and go to 203.0.113.9 instead. This is used to make a link start with a trusted name.

findings.title: Not encrypted (http, not https)
findings.explanation: Anything typed on this page would travel unencrypted. The reverse does not hold: most phishing sites use https today, so a padlock does not mean a site is genuine.

findings.title: Contains words common in phishing links
findings.explanation: The link contains login. Phishing links lean on words about logins, accounts and urgency; genuine sites use them too, so this only adds weight to other signals.
